text.p: Programme of soccer matches when the German first division resumes action after its winter break this weekend.
Friday (kickoffs 1900 GMT, figures in parenthesis indicate league position)

Borussia Dortmund (2) v Bayer Leverkusen (3). Champions Dortmund without injured international midfielder Steffen Freund and Brazilian Julio Cesar but squad fresh from 10-day training camp in Portugal. Leverkusen have looked sharp in friendlies and expect to have no injury problems.

Cologne (7) v Fortuna Duesseldorf (15). Cologne have injury doubts about Romanian forward Ion Vladoiu (pulled muscle) and striker Holger Gaissmayer (groin operation). Vladoiu's probable replacement is Stefan Kohn. Fortuna's form has been improving steadily in their series of friendlies.

Bayern Munich (1) v St. Pauli (14). Chairman Franz Beckenbauer says he wants to see more entertaining football in second half and Bayern have been working hard in training camp. Bayern expected to keep Lothar Matthaeus at libero despite talk he might return to midfield. Lowly St. Pauli should be there for the taking.

Duisburg (10) v Bochum (6). Bochum were the surprise team of first half but build-up has been hit by injury. Duisburg finished the first half strongly but have not been very impressive in recent friendlies.

Schalke (8) v VfB Stuttgart (4). Stuttgart have a real task on their hands to repeat their excellent form in the first half but winter break training camps in southern Europe have gone well with no major injuries. But Schalke are difficult opponents in front of their own fanatical supporters.

Karlsruhe (5) v Hansa Rostock (16). Injured German international midfielder Thomas Haessler unlikely to return to action for Karlsruhe before March but Germany's impressive new striker Sean Dundee in good form. Rostock players should be fully fit.

Werder Bremen (9) v Freiburg (18). Werder can field best team with Euro 96 success Dieter Eilts expected to take on new role as libero. Freiburg had a terrible first half of the season and need dramatic improvement in form.
Hamburg (11) v 1860 Munich (13). Hamburg went to Florida to prepare for restart but their defence has looked a bit hesitant in friendlies. 1860 need good start to get clear of relegation zone.

Arminia Bielefeld (12) v Borussia Moenchengladbach (17). Moenchengladbach were major disappointment in first half of season but Swedish striker Martin Dahlin and playmaker Stefan Effenberg back from injury to begin major campaign to avoid the drop. After poor start Bielefeld had a good run at the end of first half and start the second half in good physical shape.
